ARMIS_SITE_ID.description: Server-side Armis site predicate forwarded into the ASQ (Armis Search Query) ?aql= query-string parameter as siteId:<value> on GET /api/v1/devices/ and GET /api/v1/alerts/. Optional; empty / blank walks the entire tenant's inventory across every site (the dispatcher's token scope still applies). Forwarded verbatim — Armis accepts both numeric site ids (e.g. siteId:7) and the literal site name (e.g. siteId:HQ) in the siteId predicate slot depending on tenant configuration. Useful for sharding inventory pulls across multiple discovery profiles so each dispatcher agent only walks one site's worth of inventory per run. Whitespace is trimmed.

ARMIS_BOUNDARY.description: Server-side Armis boundary predicate forwarded into the ASQ ?aql= query-string parameter as boundary:"<value>" on GET /api/v1/devices/ and GET /api/v1/alerts/. Optional; empty / blank walks every boundary in the site. Boundary values are double-quoted to allow spaces / special characters (e.g. ARMIS_BOUNDARY='Corporate Network'). When combined with ARMIS_SITE_ID the two predicates compose into aql=in:devices,siteId:<id>,boundary:"<value>" so the dispatcher only walks one site / boundary's worth of inventory per agent run. Whitespace is trimmed.

name: armis
title: Armis
description: Armis CPS (Cyber-Physical Systems) asset-inventory importer. Pulls discovered devices and security alerts from an Armis console via the Armis v1 REST API and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON. Each Armis device becomes one Faraday host (the device's ipAddress projects onto host.ip — loopback / 0.0.0.0 / ::1 are explicitly skipped, the executor falls back to the first usable entry in ipv6 and then to the 0.0.0.0 sentinel; the name / hostName / fqdn projection lands on host.hostnames; macAddress lands on host.mac; and the operatingSystem / operatingSystemVersion / manufacturer / model chain joins onto host.os). Each Armis alert becomes one Faraday host keyed on the alert's ip field when device-keyed (alerts can travel with the affected device's primary IP) or the 0.0.0.0 sentinel otherwise; the title / policyTitle projection lands on host.hostnames and the alert description / severity / mitreAttackTechniques enrichment is embedded in the vulnerability description. The asset itself becomes one Faraday vulnerability with the [ASSET-INVENTORY] engine prefix so the data lands in the Faraday workspace alongside the other CMDB-class feeds (Axonius, Device42, Fleet, runZero, Jamf Pro, Jira Insight). Endpoints used: GET /api/v1/devices/?aql=<asq>&from=N&length=M (paginated device inventory; returns the canonical Armis envelope {"data": {"results": [...], "count": N, "total": N, "next": K|null}, "success": true} with each record carrying id, category, type, firstSeen, lastSeen, ipAddress, ipv6, macAddress, name, hostName, manufacturer, model, operatingSystem, operatingSystemVersion, riskLevel, siteId, siteName, boundary, purdueLevel, tags, userIds), and GET /api/v1/alerts/?aql=<asq>&from=N&length=M (the Armis security alert feed; same envelope shape with each record carrying alertId, title, description, severity, time, status, type, ip, policyId, policyTitle, siteId, siteName, mitreAttackTechniques, cveList, deviceIds, affectedDevicesCount). ARMIS_SITE_ID and ARMIS_BOUNDARY are forwarded as ASQ predicates appended to the aql query parameter on both surfaces; the ASQ in: prefix is set per-surface (in:devices for the devices walk, in:alerts for the alerts walk). Walked page-by-page (from += length per request) until len(results) < length or ARMIS_PAGES (env-only override, default 5, clamped to [1, 50]) is reached. length is fixed at 100 (Armis' documented default page size; the hard cap is 1000 but smaller pages keep response sizes manageable). Severity is always info because Armis device hits are inventory entries and Armis alerts surface as inventory-side observations that operators correlate against the EDR / EASM / vuln-scanner agents' findings via the Armis-Id / Armis-Site / Armis-Boundary / Armis-Type / Armis-RiskLevel / Armis-LastSeen / Armis-Tags / Armis-PurdueLevel refs on device hits, and the Armis-AlertId / Armis-Policy / Armis-Status / Armis-Severity / Armis-Time / Armis-Type / Armis-MITRE / Armis-DeviceCount refs on alert hits. Auth: Armis v1 uses a two-step auth flow — the dispatcher carries a long-lived ARMIS_SECRET_KEY (generated in the Armis console under Settings -> Users & Roles -> Access Tokens), and on every executor run we exchange it for a short-lived access token via POST /api/v1/access_token/ with secret_key=<key> form data. The access token returned under data.access_token travels on every subsequent /api/v1/ request as the Authorization: <token> header — Armis does NOT use the Bearer prefix on this header, the raw token IS the header value. ARMIS_HOST is the operator's tenant host (e.g. mycorp.armis.com); on-prem appliances are tolerated and https:// is added automatically when the operator pasted in a bare FQDN. Tags: [armis, asset-inventory, device|alert].
